author: end-to-end-soundness
body_markdown: The bound $D=O_\theta(d)$ is doing two independent jobs: it makes the accepted whole-relation cleanup cost $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable below $\epsilon$, and it bounds the factor list by $O_\theta(1)$. If $D$ acquires an inverse power of $\epsilon$, `E2E-20` and `E2E-21` both fail and the longer factorwise/cross-factor route is again necessary.
subject: Why bounded weight closes both losses
